sources.citation: Carter, John, John Grummitt, Janell Masters & Brian Paris. 2014. A sociolinguistic survey of the Watut languages. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2014-006.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Checked only for identity: covers South/Middle/North Watut [mcy, mpl, una]; never mentions Kapin or Leaders, consistent with Leaders' 'Middle Watut' being Kapin [tbx] and not mpl.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid kapi1250 and reference 137118; Glottolog record for ISO mpl (midd1327 Middle Watut)
sources.note: Classification Buang linkage (subclassification after Ross 1988:132-159); the two Leaders refs carry language code Kapin [tbx] from the SIL bibliography; no descriptive work beyond them.

sources.citation: OLAC 'Resources in and about the Kapin language' (tbx), up to date 2025-11-04 (the Internet Archive 2026-02-08); SIL archive search for tbx (the Internet Archive 2015-09-18); OLAC page for Middle Watut [mpl]; Ethnologue free page for tbx (the Internet Archive 2023)
sources.note: Complete inventory of catalogued resources for tbx: PARADISEC MR1-008 'Kapin Mangga' (Malcolm Ross 1980 audio), the three 2002 SIL alphabet-workshop items, the two Leaders papers; nothing else. No phonology, grammar or dictionary exists in any catalogue. Alternate names: Garawa, Gawawa, Katumene, Sambio, Taiak, Tayek. Ethnologue notes Bible portions 2015-2020.

sources.note: Kapin is named once, as a neighbouring Buang group ('To the east are the Buang language groups of Kapin, Galawo, Dumbi, Zenag and Yanta'); no Kapin data and no stress statement. Its 'Middle Watut' phoneme sketch (sec. 4.2.7) is a different language (midd1327 [mpl]).

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Kapin appears only as cognate-set data (from Hooley 1971) and in the Buang-family consonant reflex table (Kapin p v b m my); no synchronic stress statement.

sources.citation: Adams, Karen & Linda Lauck. 1985. Dialect survey of Mumeng dialect chain. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 22 (Pacific Linguistics A-63), 1-27. DOI 10.15144/PL-A63.1
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.3 'Phonological variations' (p. 11) gives a shared consonant/vowel inventory for the whole survey area and one stress remark that concerns Patep vs Kumalu/Mumengtein/Pelenkwa ('Initial unstressed syllables in Patep always have the vowel schwa.. Kumalu, Mumengtein, and Pelenkwa have a different stress pattern, so that not only does the initial syllable have a full vowel, but it also receives stress') -- nothing said about Kapin. Appendix B (pp. 16-26) has ~100-item phonetic wordlists for Kapin, Taiak and Garawa with stress marks (e.g. Kapin 'nElu 'nose', mba'mbo 'stomach', sa'kwaiN, ndE…

sources.note: 'Not Available Online'. The record settles identity: 'This paper was originally published as "Conjunctions in Middle Watut of Papua New Guinea". In a different language family, Middle Watut is located in the lower Watut river valley, and now is referred to as Middle Kodut (iso 639-3 code mpl). This article refers to tbx:Kapin, spoken in Kapin I, Kapin II, Tayek, Garawa, and Sambio.' Subject: conjunctions; no phonology expected.
